questions.question: 1. What is recursion in computer programming?

answers.b: A function with no return value

explanations.c: Correct. Recursion is when a function calls itself.
explanations.a: Incorrect. That is function composition, not recursion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Return value is not related to recursion.

questions.question: 2. Which of the following is essential for a recursive function to work correctly?

explanations.d: Correct. A base case prevents infinite recursion.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Loops are not required for recursion.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Global variables are not required.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Print statements are not required.

questions.question: 3. What will happen if a recursive function does not have a base case?

answers.b: It will run infinitely or cause a stack overflow

explanations.b: Correct. Without a base case, recursion never stops and causes a stack overflow.
explanations.d: Incorrect. It does not return 0 by default.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Output is not guaranteed to be nothing.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Infinite recursion is not faster.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following problems is best solved using recursion?

answers.b: Assigning a value to a variable

explanations.c: Correct. Factorial is a classic recursive problem.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Printing does not require recursion.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Addition is a simple operation.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Assignment does not require recursion.

questions.question: 5. What is the base case in the recursive computation of factorial(n)?

explanations.b: Correct. The factorial of 0 is defined as 1, which is the base case.
explanations.a: Incorrect. n == 1 is not the standard base case, though factorial(1) = 1.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Factorial is not defined for negative numbers.
explanations.c: Incorrect. n > 1 is not a base case.

questions.question: 6. Which of the following best describes the call stack in recursion?

answers.d: A structure that keeps track of active function calls

explanations.d: Correct. The call stack tracks recursive calls.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Variables are not the call stack.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Loops are not the call stack.

questions.question: 7. Which of the following is a disadvantage of recursion?

answers.b: It can use more memory due to the call stack
answers.a: It always runs faster than iteration
answers.c: It is never used in practice

explanations.b: Correct. Recursion can use more memory than iteration.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Recursion is not always faster.

questions.question: 8. Which of the following is an example of a divide-and-conquer algorithm that uses recursion?

explanations.b: Incorrect. Assignment is not an algorithm.
explanations.c: Correct. Merge Sort is a classic recursive algorithm.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Linear Search is usually iterative.

answers.a: A recursive call inside a loop
answers.b: A recursive call with multiple parameters
answers.c: A recursive call with no base case
answers.d: A recursive call that is the last operation in the function

explanations.b: Incorrect. Parameters do not define tail recursion.
explanations.d: Correct. Tail recursion means the recursive call is the last thing executed.

questions.question: 10. Which of the following problems can be solved using recursion?

explanations.a: Correct. Balancing weights is solved recursively.
explanations.b: Correct. Tower of Hanoi is solved recursively.
explanations.c: Correct. All of these can be solved using recursion.
explanations.d: Correct. Fibonacci sequence is solved recursively.
